PRIMITIVE.name: The Standby
PRIMITIVE.summary: The umbrella system + always-on state for *temporary centralized disruptions* — drought, fire, smoke, flood, ice, power, water, freight, payment systems, pandemic, evacuation, AGM-postponed, key-person-down. One name that holds both the slow side (always-on preparation) and the fast side (active event).
PRIMITIVE.hostZoneRationale: Hosted in Zone 3 (community production) because that is where centralized disruptions are felt collectively. The co-op shelf, the producer pipeline, the orders ledger are where the absence of freight, power, or staff lands first. Read by every zone.

subShelves.name: The Common Pantry
subShelves.role: the food/supply sub-noun — the literal shelf inside the Standby that holds staples, water, fuel, medicine. Sub-noun, not replacement.

subShelves.name: The Watch
subShelves.role: the active-monitoring sub-noun — the posture and the people doing the watching during advisory/standby rungs. Sub-noun, not replacement.

rejectedAlternatives.name: The Common Pantry (as the umbrella name)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Holds the slow side beautifully (a pantry is by definition always-on) but cannot hold an active fire call, an evacuation, or a payment-systems outage without straining the metaphor. A pantry is what you keep; the Standby is also what you do. The Pantry sits *inside* the Standby as the food/supply sub-shelf.

rejectedAlternatives.name: The Watch (as the umbrella name)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Holds the active-monitoring posture (the watch is active by definition) but cannot hold the slow shelf of standby stock without bending into something that sounds like a permanent vigil. The Watch sits *inside* the Standby as the active-monitoring sub-noun.

PRIMITIVE.scope: naming and filing only — no UI surface for tracking calls, watches, or debriefs is built on this pass. Future task once the vocabulary has been used in the field.

ITEMS.text: Glance at standby stock — what would we draw on first?
ITEMS.detail: Open the cupboard, the freezer, the medicine drawer. No re-stock yet — just see what's there.

ITEMS.text: Note what's running low (water, fuel, meds, batteries).
Read the latest advisory from the agency that issued it.
ITEMS.detail: One source, read fully. Don't doomscroll — pick the issuing agency and stay there.

ITEMS.text: Tell the household, in one sentence, what's forming.
ITEMS.detail: Kids included. The advisory is informed; the posture hasn't changed yet.

ITEMS.text: Top up water on hand — 4 L per person per day for at least 3 days.
ITEMS.detail: Drinking, cooking, basic hygiene. Fill jugs and the bath if a shutoff is plausible.

ITEMS.text: Verify fuel for heat and the generator — and test-start the generator.
ITEMS.detail: Wood stacked, propane tank weight, jerry can full. A generator that won't start is not standby stock.

ITEMS.text: Refill meds you're low on — keep a 7-day buffer for everyone in the house.
ITEMS.detail: Prescription and over-the-counter. Note expiry on anything in the kit.

ITEMS.text: Check the first-aid kit, headlamps, batteries, hand-crank radio.
Set aside small bills (cash) in case payment systems are down.
Confirm the kid-care plan — who picks up if school closes mid-day.
ITEMS.detail: Primary, backup, and the third name if both are at work. Tell the kids who.

ITEMS.text: Print the contact tree — who calls whom, on paper, not just in phones.
ITEMS.detail: Stick it on the fridge. Phones die; the fridge does not.

ITEMS.text: Agree on a meeting place if the household gets separated.
ITEMS.detail: One indoor, one outdoor. Tell every person, not just the adults.

ITEMS.text: Charge phones and the backup battery; queue a paper map of the route out.
Pet & livestock plan — food, water, and an evacuation route for them too.
Name the neighbour who'd struggle most — the elder, the household alone with kids.
ITEMS.detail: Decide who in your household checks on them when a call opens.

ITEMS.text: Open the call: pull standby stock out where the household can see it.
ITEMS.detail: Counter, table, hallway. What's hidden in a cupboard is not in the call.

ITEMS.text: Ration water at 4 L per person per day; log what's used.
ITEMS.detail: A line on a sheet of paper is enough. The log is for the debrief.

ITEMS.text: Run the generator on a schedule — don't leave it on or run the tank dry.
Take meds at normal times. A call is not a reason to skip a dose.
Trigger the contact tree once — not five times.
ITEMS.detail: One message, the named callers make their named calls.

ITEMS.text: Confirm everyone is at the meeting place — or accounted for by name.
Stay on one weather/agency channel; mute the rest.
ITEMS.detail: Pick the agency that issued the advisory. Information overload is a posture problem.

ITEMS.text: Check on the neighbour you named at standby.
Replenish standby stock — water, meds, fuel, batteries, first-aid.
ITEMS.detail: Replace what was used before the call closes in your head, or it won't get done.

ITEMS.text: Reset the fridge contact-tree printout if it got drawn on or torn.
Close the contact tree — one message: standdown.
Write the debrief: what worked, what didn't, what we'd reset.
ITEMS.detail: Five lines is plenty. The debrief is the artifact the household keeps.

ITEMS.text: Send the debrief to the co-op so the cross-zone record holds.
ITEMS.detail: Optional, never required. The household keeps a copy either way.
